title: Read and rank access levels

blocks.text: The page orders the access levels from most to least restrictive: **private > default (package-private) > protected > public**.
Write three methods of the enum `AccessLevel`:

items: `static AccessLevel of(int modifiers)` reads the level out of the bit set that `java.lang.reflect.Member.getModifiers()` or `Class.getModifiers()` returns. Use the helpers in `java.lang.reflect.Modifier`.
`boolean isMoreRestrictiveThan(AccessLevel other)` answers whether this level allows access to fewer places than `other`.
`static AccessLevel mostRestrictive(AccessLevel first, AccessLevel... rest)` returns the most restrictive of the levels given.

blocks.text: The constants are declared in alphabetical order, which is **not** the order of restrictiveness.

of(Modifier.PUBLIC)                                 -> PUBLIC
of(Modifier.STATIC | Modifier.FINAL)                -> PACKAGE
PACKAGE.isMoreRestrictiveThan(PUBLIC)               -> true
mostRestrictive(PUBLIC, PROTECTED)                  -> PROTECTED

cases.says: A member declared public, protected or private is read as that level.
A member with no access keyword is package-private, even when it carries other modifiers such as static or final.
Of several levels, private is the most restrictive and public the least.
Package-private is more restrictive than protected, because protected adds subclasses in other packages.

concepts: A member declared with no access keyword is package-private.
From most to least restrictive the levels run private, package-private, protected, public.
